absent: Virtual mapping establishment and teardown for counter access plus address discovery from firmware tables.
Full register offsets and bit definitions for global and per channel configuration beyond sanitized bits visible here.
Frequency conversion edge handling and clock event selection plus platform timer reservation policy.
Hotplug online and offline actions for event channels and their failure recovery.
Resume counter behavior and suspend path interaction with timekeeping.
Virtual 8086 owner table management, signal selection, and line re enable path after consumption.
Performance event object lifecycle, scheduling across tasks, and slot exhaustion handling beyond local failure.
Kprobe blacklist predicate, range breakpoint hardware semantics, and feature detection for extension support.

findings.text: A shared eight byte cell offers two views of identical storage. One view couples a low level spin primitive with a cached 32 bit counter copy. The other view exposes the whole as one 64 bit word so both members can be observed together. The global instance resides on its own cache line and starts released with a cleared cache.

Provides a recent counter sample without blocking non maskable context and without exposing torn updates. The non maskable path observes hardware directly. The uncontended path refreshes a shared cached copy under interrupt masking and mutual exclusion. The contended path performs no update and only waits for progress indicated by cache advance or release, ensuring callers always receive either a fresh observation or a recently stored one.

Joint word reads use single atomic observation. Updates to the cached copy occur only while holding the spin primitive with interrupts masked, using a non tearing store, followed by release before unmasking. Contended observers never attempt acquisition and only poll the joint word, so at most one updater exists and readers cannot deadlock against interrupt context.

Direct hardware consultation in non maskable context avoids self deadlock if the primitive is owned. A torn cached store would corrupt concurrent snapshots, hence atomic store discipline matters. A stale snapshot taken just before release could otherwise force needless waiting, so the waiter also accepts release as progress.

An alternate reader variant offers no caching and no synchronization. Every invocation consults the hardware counter directly and widens the result, suitable where external serialization already exists or contention handling is undesired.

The timekeeping descriptor binds the guarded reader as its sampling hook and a dedicated resume routine as its restore hook. It advertises continuous operation across suspend and prior calibration, delegating frequency discovery to the enable flow.
Clocksource identity facts are name hpet, rating 250, mask from HPET_MASK, and flags combining continuous with calibrated.

Configuration sanity requires observing any value other than all ones within one thousand polls, otherwise the device is abandoned. Liveness requires restarting the counter and then observing a tick change within two hundred thousand processor cycles, otherwise the device is abandoned.

Deep package sleep damage is reported only on Intel parts with monitor wait support where processor identification advertises extension and break capabilities plus a non empty high substate nibble, and where the package sleep limit control permits the deepest state. A user force override suppresses the damage verdict with a warning, otherwise a positive verdict records a boot disable and logs an informational note.

Bring up proceeds through screening, mapping, validation, discovery and publication. Screening rejects incapable or sleep damaged hardware. Mapping must yield an address. Validation checks configuration liveness and period plausibility and derives frequency from the period. Discovery learns channel count and enforces a two channel minimum when RTC emulation is selected, allocates per channel records, preserves boot copies while clearing enable and mode bits and reporting unknown bits, then rechecks liveness. Publication registers the time source and, when legacy support is present, assigns legacy roles to initial channels. Any validation or allocation failure releases records, clears mapping and address, and reports absence.

Late initialization accepts a forced address when no address was discovered, reattempting enable in that case. It then requires a mapped address, performs device channel choice, event choice and platform timer reservation, and when event channels exist it registers online and dead hotplug handlers, removing the online handler if dead registration fails.
RTC emulation defaults are periodic frequency 64, shift 6, and interrupt count per tick 1.

Emulation retains enable flags, previous update second with negative meaning none yet, alarm hour minute second, periodic tick accumulator, last programmed comparator, default delta, periodic delta, divisor for slow rates, and a single registered callback slot initially empty.
Ahead testing interprets the unsigned difference of two 32 bit counter values as signed, reporting ahead when the result is negative, which correctly handles wrap.
Early initialization entry reports one when legacy clock event setup occurred and zero when the timer is unusable or unavailable, performing full discovery and cleanup internally.

Callback registration fails when the timer is disabled and fails as busy when a callback is already present, otherwise it stores the supplied handler and reports success. Unregistration clears both the handler slot and all enable flags when the timer is enabled and does nothing otherwise.

Timer start derives a default interval from event scaling on first use. It selects the default interval unless periodic mode with no divisor is active, in which case it uses the periodic interval. Under interrupt masking it programs a comparator ahead of the current count, records that value, and enables the channel in 32 bit non periodic mode. Disabling only clears the enable bit.

Masking clears requested enable bits and stops the channel when no bits remain. Setting adds bits, resets update tracking on rising update enable, and lazily starts the timer when moving from empty to non empty. Alarm setting stores hour minute second. Frequency setting uses a divisor for rates at or below the default and otherwise computes a fresh periodic interval from event scaling.

Rearm advances the stored comparator by the chosen interval and reprograms until it lies ahead of the counter, counting iterations beyond the first as missed ticks. Missed periodic ticks accumulate and a rate limited warning may appear. Interrupt handling first rearms, conditionally refreshes wall time, derives update periodic and alarm indications with first update suppression and divisor gating, merges them with status and count, and invokes the registered callback when any indication exists.
The RTC emulation interrupt entry always claims the interrupt. It rearms the channel and reports update periodic and alarm conditions through the registered callback with status and count encoding.

The virtual 8086 interrupt entry records a pending edge for its line, delivers a configured signal to the owning task, and suspends the line until userspace consumes the pending state. Duplicate edges and lines without owners are ignored.

Pending bits and owner lookup are protected by a spin primitive held with interrupts saved. Ownership and duplication checks, bit setting, and line suspension all occur under that guard, with distinct return codes for claimed versus ignored edges.

Each processor retains its own debug control copy, an array of address copies sized by the breakpoint count, and an array of occupant slots of the same size initially empty. The control copy mirrors the hardware control register for non maskable visibility.

Per register control combines a four bit length plus type field placed at a control base plus a per register stride, together with a global enable bit placed at a per register enable stride. The public encoder additionally sets a global slowdown bit. Decoding reverses the placement to recover generic length and type markers and the enable pair.

Installation finds a free occupant slot, records the owner, programs the address copy and hardware address, merges the encoded control into the processor control copy, orders the copy before the hardware update, then applies an address mask when present. Removal clears the occupant slot, removes the encoding from the control snapshot, updates hardware and mask first, orders before publishing the control copy, ensuring non maskable observers never see an inconsistent pair.

Slot search, address programming and control updates require interrupts disabled on the local processor and operate only on local per CPU state, so no cross processor locking is needed. A compiler ordering barrier separates control copy publication from hardware updates in opposite directions for install versus removal.

Length translation accepts one two four and eight byte sizes on 64 bit, rejecting others. Execute type requires the architecture undefined length and maps to instruction type with word sized length. Write maps to write only and read write maps to combined access, both then requiring successful length translation.

Kernel membership holds when the start address or its inclusive end reaches the user limit, with overflow excluded by alignment. Overlap holds when an interval end reaches a region base while its start precedes the region end.

Breakpoints overlapping processor entry mappings, per processor offset tables, guest descriptor tables, task state, translation state, or the retained debug control copy risk unwanted debug faults or entry corruption and must be rejected. Range checks cover every possible processor for the per processor regions.

If the counter overtakes the programmed comparator before rearm, multiple intervals may elapse. The rearm loop catches up by repeated advancement and accounts the extra expirations as lost, preventing a stuck behind comparator.

Construction rejects address length overflow and forbidden overlap, then maps type and length. Instruction breakpoints in kernel space are refused when blacklisted and otherwise require word sized length. Data range mode requires power of two aligned length plus range extension support and records a mask with unit length. Final parsing derives an alignment mask from length or mask and rejects misaligned addresses.
Timer control exports report one when emulation is active and zero when disabled. They cover timer start, flag mask and set, alarm store, and periodic frequency selection.

Architecture breakpoint exports provide control encoding and decoding, slot install and removal, generic field translation, kernel membership testing, and attribute parsing with alignment enforcement.
